seo.title: OPSYS-AI
seo.seo_title: OPSYS-AI: AI software for construction companies
seo.seo_description: OPSYS-AI coordinates ten virtual departments for construction companies, from the first request to the draft invoice, with an honest status for each capability.

blocks.role: Promise from brief §7; calls to action for a demonstration and a deployment study.

translation.headline: A coordinated team for your construction company.
translation.subheadline: Ten virtual departments work on the same files, from the first request to the preparation of the invoice. Every capability states its status: available, pilot or planned.

translation.title: What costs you time.
translation.body:
Often, a construction company does not lack tools: it lacks links between them. The request sits in an inbox, the quote in a spreadsheet, the job on paper sheets, the invoice in the accounting system.

OPSYS-AI starts from that observation: one file, several departments, one logical sequence.

items.title: Requests arrive everywhere.
items.text: Phone, email, web form: nothing guarantees that a request will be followed up.

items.title: Quotes take time.
items.text: Information is missing, quantities are re-entered, margins are worked out separately.

items.title: The job ends, the invoice lags.
items.text: Hours, materials and photos are pulled together after the fact.

items.title: Actual costs arrive too late.
items.text: Estimate and actual are compared once the job is already closed.

items.title: Decisions get lost.
items.text: Why this price, this supplier, this delay? Nobody remembers.

blocks.role: Overall journey: five stages that group the ten departments.

translation.title: One file. Ten departments.
translation.body:
Instead of ten isolated tools, a single file follows the request from end to end. Each department reads what the others have prepared and adds its share, through an internal event bus: a shared log where each department notes what has just happened.

What the system prepares, a person approves. Sending, paying, deciding: these actions wait for your go-ahead.

items.title: Receive and sell.
items.text: Intake, customer relations, estimating and quoting (M1 to M3).

items.title: Plan and deliver.
items.text: Field work and materials: crews, schedules, proof of work, needs and receipts (M4 and M6).

items.title: Invoice.
items.text: Draft invoice, receivables and actual costs (M5).

items.title: Grow and steer.
items.text: Marketing, analytics and strategy (M7 to M9).

items.title: Remember.
items.text: Memory of decisions and of authorized knowledge (M10).

blocks.role: The ten departments M1 to M10, with the honest status taken from report 07.

translation.title: The ten departments.
translation.intro: Each card states its status. Available: the software does it today. Pilot: it works, with limits that we spell out. Planned: not delivered yet.

cards.title: M1 — Intake.
cards.text:
Centralizes and qualifies requests, prepares follow-ups and hands off to the right person with the context.
Available: request qualification (to be configured for your company), handoffs to a human, missed calls logged by your team. Pilot: transcribed voicemails. Planned: replies sent to the customer, real-time voice intake.

cards.title: M2 — Customer relations and sales.
cards.text:
Tracks contacts, files, quotes and follow-ups, and suggests the next action.
Available: file creation from a request, suggested next action. Pilot: file tracking, follow-ups, duplicate detection. Planned: connection to an external customer relationship management (CRM) system, visual tracking board (kanban).

cards.title: M3 — Estimating.
cards.text:
Prepares an estimate and a quote from the information provided, shows what is missing and refuses to give a figure when the information is insufficient.
Status: available for the calculation and the draft quote, pilot for the rest. Quantities and prices are entered by your team. The quote is a draft, stripped of your internal costs and margins. Planned: measurement from photos.

cards.title: M4 — Field operations.
cards.text:
Organizes crews, schedules, jobs, time and proof of completion.
Available: a job created from an accepted quote. Pilot: scheduling by route, clock-in at server time, after photos, signature and checklist. Planned: location at clock-in, road routing, automatic dispatch.

cards.title: M5 — FinanceCore.
cards.text:
Prepares invoicing, financial tracking, costs and analyses, with appropriate approvals.
Available: draft invoice after the job, accounts receivable, accounts payable entered by your team. Pilot: cash-flow forecast, actual cost per job, reconciliation from exported statements. Payroll is prepared (hours and gross pay) for your accountant, without payroll calculation. Planned: sending invoices, bank and accounting connections. The tax calendar must be validated by your accountant.

cards.title: M6 — Materials.
cards.text:
Links needs, availability, suppliers, orders, receipts and actual consumption.
Available: needs forecast from an accepted quote, reservations, gap between estimated and actual quantities. Pilot: approved draft purchase order, receipts, losses and breakage. Planned: sending the order to the supplier. This department makes no payments.

cards.title: M7 — Marketing.
cards.text:
Turns authorized information into content proposals and tracks where your customers come from.
Status: available once your brand is configured, pilot for the rest. Proposals are submitted for your approval and consent is verified; export to your channels is manual. Pilot: tracking from request to quote to margin, with no advertising cost for now. Review requests remain drafts. Planned: automatic publishing to social networks.

cards.title: M8 — Analytics.
cards.text:
Makes indicators understandable, sourced and accompanied by their quality: an indicator shows “not calculable” when data is missing.
Available: executive view. Pilot: per-job measures. Planned: forecasts, health score.

cards.title: M9 — Strategy.
cards.text:
Gathers the information that management needs for priorities and for tracking decisions.
Available: management briefing and strategic reading, which inform without advising. Pilot: tracking a decision under the owner's approval, which executes nothing. Planned: scenarios, priorities and objectives.

cards.title: M10 — Memory.
cards.text:
Retrieves decisions and authorized knowledge, with their context and their sources.
Status: available for the log of decisions and events, which detects any modification; pilot for searching the company's knowledge, disabled by default. Planned: relationship graph between files.

blocks.role: Central demonstration, link by link: real / demonstration / target.

translation.title: From request to invoice.
translation.body:
This is the central journey as it stands today. For each link: what is real (the software does it), what is a demonstration (fictitious data or a partly simulated application) and what is a target (not delivered yet).

Four states are never confused: prepared, approved, sent, acknowledged. Verification was carried out on fictitious data.

items.title: 1. Request received.
items.text: Real: the intake engine, tested on fictitious data. Demonstration: SMS transport and telephony. Prepared: a summary of the request.

items.title: 2. Qualification.
items.text: Real, to be configured for your company: score, questions, next action, handoff to a human.

items.title: 3. Customer file.
items.text: Real: the file is created from the qualified request. Full file tracking is in pilot.

items.title: 4. Estimate.
items.text: Real: the calculation, which refuses to give a figure without sufficient information. Quantities and prices are entered. Target: measurement from photos.

items.title: 5. Approved quote.
items.text: Real: draft quote, eleven-criteria review and approval. Prepared and approved, yes; sent and acknowledged, no. Target: sending to the customer.

items.title: 6. Scheduling and materials.
items.text: Real on the server side, without a screen: job to schedule, schedule, reservation, approved draft purchase order. Target: sending the purchase order to the supplier.

items.title: 7. Execution.
items.text: Real: job completion on the server side. Demonstration: the employee app, whose clock-in uses a fictitious location.

items.title: 8. Controlled close-out.
items.text: Real on the server side: the completed job waits for a review and the material gap is calculated in quantities. Target: the alert on the administrator's phone.

items.title: 9. Draft invoice.
items.text: Real, internally: a draft invoice is prepared, with GST and QST calculated, to be validated by your accountant. Prepared, yes; sent and acknowledged, no.

items.title: 10. Analysis and tracking.
items.text: Real: executive view, management briefing, log of decisions. Demonstration: comparison of estimate and actual, on fictitious data.

blocks.role: Signature scenario “job completed”, link by link.

translation.title: When the job is done.
translation.body: The signature scenario. The employee enters photos, time, checklist and materials. Gaps trigger a review. The departments concerned prepare their updates. Here, link by link, is what is real, a demonstration or a target today.

items.title: The employee finishes the job.
items.text: Demonstration: the checklist is local, after photos go into a queue, clock-in uses a fictitious location and the materials screen is not yet qualified.

items.title: A gap triggers a review.
items.text: Real on the server side: job completion moves to awaiting review and requires a manager's approval.

items.title: Materials are compared.
items.text: Real: estimated and actual quantities compared, withdrawals recorded, low stock flagged. Prices are not yet taken into account.

items.title: The draft invoice is prepared.
items.text: Real, internally: draft invoice and updated profitability. Target: PDF, numbering and sending.

items.title: The customer file is updated.
items.text: Real: the job is marked complete and the activity is written. The next action is only a suggestion.

items.title: Content is proposed.
items.text: Real once your brand is configured: content proposals submitted for your decision, manual export. The review request remains a draft, never sent.

items.title: Estimate is compared to actual.
items.text: Demonstration: comparison in minutes, on fictitious data. Dollars are not yet compared.

items.title: Results are exposed.
items.text: Real: executive view. Pilot: job measures.

items.title: The event is kept.
items.text: Real: the log of decisions and events, which detects any modification, keeps the event and its sources.

items.title: The customer is kept informed.
items.text: Target: message to the customer, sending the invoice, acknowledgment. No real sending exists today.

blocks.role: Differentiators: estimate versus actual, materials, finance, cash, agents and budgets, memory.

translation.title: What sets it apart.
translation.intro: Not a robot that answers the phone: departments that share the same file.

cards.title: Estimate against actual.
cards.text: Estimated quantities are compared with actual quantities after every job (available). So are minutes, on fictitious data (demonstration).

cards.title: Materials before the job.
cards.text: Needs are calculated as soon as the quote is accepted. The order is prepared and approved, then sent by your team: no automatic sending to the supplier.

cards.title: Invoicing without re-entry.
cards.text: The draft invoice comes from the job data. You validate it; sending stays with your team.

cards.title: The balance and what you owe.
cards.text: Spendable cash is the money actually available once known obligations are deducted. It relies on your internal ledger, not on a bank connection (pilot).

cards.title: Agents bounded by a budget.
cards.text: Each agent has a profile, permissions and a token budget (a token is the unit of text a model processes), checked before the call to a provider. The budget is counted in tokens, not dollars (pilot).

cards.title: A log of decisions.
cards.text: Why this price, this supplier, this delay? Decisions are logged with their context, in a register that detects any modification.

blocks.role: Mobile: four profiles, distinct rights, offline not announced.

translation.title: Four profiles on mobile.
translation.body:
Each profile has its own rights: the owner approves, the salesperson follows customers, the employee enters field data, the customer follows their file. Today, three profiles exist in pilot; the fourth is planned.

Offline operation is designed, but it has not yet been verified against a server: we do not announce it. There are no push notifications.

items.title: Owner or administrator.
items.text: Pilot: approvals (online only) and department screens.

items.title: Salesperson.
items.text: Pilot: requests, customer record, notes and read-only quotes. No estimating, margin or photos.

items.title: Employee.
items.text: Pilot: field entry (after photos, checklist, signature) and job completion. Clock-in is yet to be qualified; the home screen is minimal.

items.title: Customer.
items.text: Planned: file tracking through secure links. Nothing is delivered.

blocks.role: Deployment and sovereignty, with no invented “sovereign mode”.

translation.title: Deployment and sovereignty, plainly.
translation.body:
OPSYS-AI installs on a server or a virtual private server (VPS) that you control. This installation is in pilot: we qualify the procedure with you.

A promise of sovereignty is proven flow by flow. OPSYS-AI goes through a model gateway that can call external AI providers, depending on the configuration. A sovereign mode, in which no business content leaves your perimeter, is not yet defined in the product: until it is, we do not announce it.

To go further: the deployment modes and our approach to sovereignty.

items.title: What we do.
items.text: For your configuration, we describe in writing where the data is, who can access it, which flows are configured and which are disabled.

items.title: What stays your decision.
items.text: Which models to use, local or external. No external service is configured without your written consent.

items.title: Backup and recovery.
items.text: Backup and restore scripts are provided (pilot). A full restore still has to be proven on your installation.

items.title: Hosting in Quebec.
items.text: Under consideration in Nexora AI's infrastructure, located in Quebec. To be qualified during the deployment study.

items.title: A protected console.
items.text: Approvals, modes and budgets are managed in a web console protected by authentication.

blocks.role: Going live: study, configuration, pilot, training, operation.

translation.title: From study to go-live.
translation.body: We announce no one-size-fits-all timeline. It depends on the number of departments activated, on your data and on your integrations, and it is measured on a pilot.

blocks.role: Les cinq étapes de la mise en service, en frise numérotée.

cards.title: Deployment study.
cards.text: We map your processes, tools and data, and choose which departments to activate first.

cards.title: Configuration.
cards.text: Brand, rate schedules, qualification rules, handoff recipients: the system is tuned to your company.

cards.title: Pilot on one flow.
cards.text: A single journey first, for example from request to quote, with your approvals.

cards.title: Training.
cards.text: Your team learns to supervise, approve and correct.

cards.title: Operation.
cards.text: We follow what works and widen the scope, department by department.

blocks.role: OPSYS-AI FAQ: objections and limits, true answers only.

items.question: Is OPSYS-AI a chatbot?
items.answer: No. It is a set of ten departments that work on the same files: request, estimate, job, materials, invoice, analysis, memory. The aim is not to chat, but to coordinate.

items.question: Are quotes and invoices sent automatically?
items.answer: No. The system prepares drafts. The quote is stripped of your internal costs and margins and goes through an approval. Real sending to the customer does not exist yet: your team transmits the document.

items.question: Are all ten departments available?
items.answer: No, and we say so department by department. Some elements are available, many are in pilot, others are planned. The cards in the “The ten departments” section give the detail.

items.question: What does human approval do?
items.answer: It blocks the binding action (sending, paying, a financial decision) until an authorized person decides. A log keeps the record.

items.question: Can we install it on our own server?
items.answer: Yes, on a server or a VPS that you control. Installation is in pilot: the procedure is qualified with us.

items.question: Is OPSYS-AI offered in a sovereign mode?
items.answer: Not under that name. We describe the real perimeter of your installation instead: where the data is, who accesses it, which flows are configured. A mode in which no business content leaves your perimeter is not yet defined in the product.

items.question: Does it connect to our accounting or our bank?
items.answer: Not today. The system prepares files for your accountant and reconciles statements that you export. Bank and accounting connections are planned, not delivered.

items.question: Are voicemails and calls handled?
items.answer: Uploaded voicemails can be transcribed (pilot). There is no real-time phone receptionist.

items.question: Does it work offline on mobile?
items.answer: Offline mode is designed, but it has not yet been verified against a server: we do not guarantee it.

items.question: How long does go-live take?
items.answer: No universal timeline is announced. It depends on the departments activated, your data and your integrations, and it is measured on a pilot.

items.question: How much does it cost?
items.answer: There is no public price. A deployment study establishes, in writing, what is included and what it costs.

items.question: Is there a free trial?
items.answer: No, not as self-service. We offer a demonstration on fictitious data, a deployment study, then a qualified pilot.

blocks.role: Final call to action: demonstration or deployment study.

translation.title: Let's talk about your jobs.
translation.text: Request a demonstration on fictitious data, or a deployment study for your company. We move with you, step by step: demonstration, study, then pilot.
